claim_checks.claim: Located in the heart of Marunouchi
claim_checks.note: Forbes places it in the Marunouchi district; the postal address is 1-8-1 Yurakucho, Chiyoda-ku, on the Marunouchi/Yurakucho edge.

claim_checks.claim: Sits directly across from the Imperial Palace East Gardens
claim_checks.note: The hotel is opposite the Imperial Palace (outer) gardens and Hibiya Park. The East Gardens are a separate area to the north, on the former Edo Castle Honmaru/Ninomaru grounds. Say 'overlooks the Imperial Palace gardens and Hibiya Park'.

claim_checks.claim: Offers rare views of 'Japan's most sacred grounds'
claim_checks.note: The palace-garden and Hibiya Park views are confirmed. 'Most sacred grounds' is editorial hyperbole.

claim_checks.claim: Rolls-Royce fleet in signature Peninsula green
claim_checks.note: Sources report two Rolls-Royce Extended Wheelbase Phantoms plus a 1934 Phantom II, and the fleet also has custom MINI Cooper S Clubmans. The green livery was not verified on a fetched page.

claim_checks.claim: Building design mirrors the palace's traditional architecture
claim_checks.note: The 24-storey tower's design concept is a traditional Japanese lantern, not the palace.
A Grand Deluxe Imperial Palace View room category exists. No source ties it to floors 20 and up.

claim_checks.claim: Unobstructed sunrise views over the Imperial Palace grounds
claim_checks.note: The palace lies west of the hotel, in the same direction as the Mount Fuji views from Peter's west-facing seats, so palace-view rooms face sunset rather than sunrise. Drop 'sunrise'.

claim_checks.claim: Within walking distance of Tokyo Station
claim_checks.note: Plausible, but not stated in the fetched sources. A verified alternative: direct basement access to the Hibiya subway station.

claim_checks.claim: Ginza shopping district just two blocks away
claim_checks.note: Forbes: Ginza is 'only a three-minute walk away'.
The East Gardens were built on Edo Castle grounds (shogunate seat from 1603) and opened to the public in October 1968. They are not a thousand years old.

claim_checks.claim: Cherry blossoms bloom in the East Gardens in spring
claim_checks.note: Not confirmed in the fetched content.

claim_checks.claim: Rooftop Peter bar offers 360-degree city views
claim_checks.note: Peter is an indoor restaurant and bar on the 24th (top) floor, not an open rooftop. Forbes describes 180-degree views. Since 1 October 2025, Peter has been a Modern French restaurant (formerly a steak and grill) with Peter: The Bar.

claim_checks.claim: Mount Fuji visible from Peter on clear days
claim_checks.note: Only a secondary source says this, referring to the west-facing seating.

claim_checks.claim: Multiple acclaimed restaurants offering Japanese and international cuisine
claim_checks.note: Hei Fung Terrace (Cantonese) is a 2025 Michelin Guide Tokyo selected restaurant. Peter is Modern French, and there is also The Lobby. No standalone Japanese restaurant was confirmed.

claim_checks.claim: Peninsula Spa featuring immersive Japanese wellness treatments
claim_checks.note: Forbes cites Asian-influenced treatments, including the shiatsu-based Keihatsu Enlightenment Massage.
The pool is indoors: a 20 m (65 ft) heated pool with a vitality pool in the 5th-floor health club, overlooking the palace gardens and Hibiya Park.
Forbes notes smart control panels and in-room nail dryers.
The hotel has no resort grounds, but Hibiya Park and the palace gardens are across the street, so this con is overstated.

facts.text: 314 rooms and suites in a 24-storey tower that opened on 1 September 2007; it is the only Peninsula hotel in Japan.
Address 1-8-1 Yurakucho, Chiyoda-ku, opposite the Imperial Palace gardens and Hibiya Park, with direct basement access to Hibiya subway station.
facts.source_title: American Express Travel - The Peninsula Tokyo

facts.text: Ginza is about a three-minute walk away.
facts.source_title: Forbes Travel Guide - The Peninsula Tokyo

facts.text: Haneda Airport is about 8.8 miles away (around 40 minutes by airport bus); Narita is about 35.7 miles (around 90 minutes by bus).
facts.source_title: American Express Travel - The Peninsula Tokyo
Forbes Travel Guide - The Peninsula Tokyo

facts.text: Peter, on the top (24th) floor, relaunched on 1 October 2025 as a Modern French restaurant under Chef Yohan Da Costa, with Peter: The Bar alongside.
facts.source_title: The Peninsula Tokyo Unveils a Modern French Dining Concept at Peter

facts.text: Hei Fung Terrace (2nd floor) serves Cantonese cuisine and is a Michelin Guide Tokyo 2025 selected restaurant.
facts.source_title: 2025 Michelin Tokyo Chinese Restaurant: Hei Fung Terrace

facts.text: Other dining: afternoon tea in The Lobby with live music, and The Peninsula Boutique & Café, known for its mango pudding.
facts.source_title: Forbes Travel Guide - The Peninsula Tokyo

facts.text: The Peninsula Spa is on the 6th floor and has a thermal suite with steam rooms, saunas and experience showers. The 5th-floor health club has a 20 m heated indoor pool and a vitality pool overlooking the palace gardens and Hibiya Park.
The house-car fleet includes Rolls-Royce Phantoms and custom MINI Cooper S Clubmans. The MINIs offer complimentary chauffeured rides for suite guests (up to 3 hours within 10 km).
facts.source_title: Japan Today - Peninsula Tokyo receives 2 MINI Cooper S Clubman cars

facts.text: More than 1,000 artworks by about 60 Japanese artists are displayed throughout; the hotel is pet-friendly and has a dog menu.
facts.source_title: Forbes Travel Guide - The Peninsula Tokyo

considerations.text: The hotel is in a dense city-centre business and shopping district (Marunouchi/Yurakucho), not a resort setting. Green space means Hibiya Park and the palace gardens across the street.
considerations.source_title: Forbes Travel Guide - The Peninsula Tokyo

considerations.text: Narita is about 90 minutes away by airport bus. Haneda (about 40 minutes) is much more convenient for this hotel.
considerations.source_title: American Express Travel - The Peninsula Tokyo

considerations.text: The pool is indoors in the 5th-floor health club. There is no rooftop or outdoor pool.
considerations.source_title: Forbes Travel Guide - The Peninsula Tokyo

considerations.text: Peter changed concept in October 2025 (steak and grill to Modern French tasting and à la carte menus). Older reviews describing a steakhouse are out of date.
Palace and park views depend on room category: the Grand Deluxe Imperial Palace View and Park View categories are booked separately from entry-level Deluxe rooms.

best_for: Luxury shoppers and first-time Tokyo visitors: about three minutes' walk to Ginza, with direct subway access at Hibiya.
Food-focused couples: Modern French tasting menus at Peter and Michelin-selected Cantonese at Hei Fung Terrace.
Business travellers: Marunouchi location, Haneda about 40 minutes by bus, and in-room tech.
Travellers with dogs: pet-friendly, with a dog menu.
